newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Jordan asks U.N. to allow Iraqi oil imports by sea.
newsitem.headline: Jordan asks U.N. to allow Iraqi oil imports by sea.

text.p: The United Nations Sanctions Committee on Iraq Wednesday deferred a decision on Jordan's request to import Iraqi oil by sea, instead of by tanker truck overland, the U.N. sanctions chariman said.

Portugal's Ambassador to the United Nations Antonio Monteiro, the sanctions committee head, said informal meetings on Jordan's request would take place next week. The issue was not deemed controversial, but would need study before action could be taken, Monteiro said.
Jordanian Ambassador Hasan Abu-Nimah formally asked the sanctions panel to allow the Iraqi imports by sea in order to save money, and noted Jordan depends on Iraqi oil for all its oil needs.

"A substantial quantity of these imports is consumed in the region of Aqaba City, particularly by the Electricity Generating Plant located at Aqaba. These needs are now in excess of 500,000 tons and are projected to grow by 250,000 tons per annum as of 1998," the Jordanian request stated.
The cost of overland transportation to the Aqaba region alone was put at $14 million per year, a figure that Jordan said could be cut by $5 million if sea shipment was approved.
Jordan said it hoped to win committee approval for Iraqi shipments from the Iraqi port of Basrah to the Jordanian port of Aqaba.

Jordan imports varying amounts of Iraqi oil as part of a deal allowing Iraq to clear debt owed to Amman, and for aid imports to Iraq. Late last year, Jordan imported around 70,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude.
